newsitem.title: USA: Higher Q2 U.S. labor costs prompt no price worries.
newsitem.headline: Higher Q2 U.S. labor costs prompt no price worries.

text.p: A modest rise in the growth rate of overall compensation costs in the second quarter does not suggest profit margins are being squeezed or companies will soon be forced to raise prices, economists said Tuesday.
"We are not getting the cost push inflation that some had feared because of the low unemployment rate," said Alison Lynn Reaser, chief econmist at Barnett Banks Inc.
The Labor Department said its Employment Cost Index rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter, a slightly faster clip than the 0.6-percent advance in the first three months of the year.
The labor cost rise was right in line with the consensus forecast. Many economists also correctly predicted that wage and salary growth would remain tame in the quarter.
Employers awarded wage and salary increases at a slower rate, 0.8 percent, than in the first quarter where they granted a more generous 0.9 percent.

"There is no acceleration evident in either the wages and salaries component or the benefits component, when you look at them on a year-on-year basis," said Dana Johnson, managing director of research at First Chicago Capital Markets.
